subject: Post-call: inference margin playbook + next steps for 1M-token targets

Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: inference margin playbook + next steps for 1M-token targets

Hi Alex — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the concrete asks we agreed to follow up on: 

Summary of what we heard
- Product: billing-and-care feature (patient triage + summary) will call the model for structured summaries and follow-up suggestions. Average tokens per invocation ~1.2k (estimate).
- Usage: target pilot cohort 10k MAUs, expected active subset ~6k -> pilot monthly token volume range: 150M–360M depending on usage patterns (conservative -> optimistic).
- Business: procurement target is Q1 (decision window ~3–6 weeks). You flagged sensitivity to unit economics (target payback and $/1M tokens).

Initial pricing/target economics (for alignment)
- Your stated target: ~$30–$45 per 1M tokens (you mentioned $/1M as a rough target band)
- Preliminary Redwood benchmark: list price for hosted SLA + support and routing policies would typically sit higher than infra-only cost; baseline anchor for discussion: $35–$50 / 1M tokens depending on model variant + latency SLOs.
- Example math (conservative): 300M tokens/mo at $40/1M => $12k/mo; at $35 => $10.5k/mo.

Unit-econ asks we promised to model
- Per-feature cost: cost to serve 1k users for the triage feature (tokens per invocation, caching potential, expected QPS).
- CAC payback: target payback window you prefer (you mentioned 6–9 months on call) — confirm exact target.
- Margin target: what gross margin % you need to hit to greenlight the product economics (common targets: 50–70%).

Attachments: I attached a short worksheet (redwood-inference-feature-econ-worksheet.xlsx) with the template we use for $/feature and payback modeling. Please fill or confirm assumptions you want us to use.

Next steps (can we lock these in?)
1) You: confirm the single-point token assumptions we should model (avg tokens per invocation, expected MAUs / DAUs).
2) Redwood: schedule a 45-min deep-dive with engineering (Karthik) + product (Marissa) to run the worksheet live and align on caching/batching levers — propose Wed or Thu next week.
3) Procurement: loop in your procurement contact so we can surface typical contract terms and procurement checklist.

As a starter question to unblock modeling — is a 6-month CAC payback target realistic for you, or should we model 9 months?

Thanks —
Rachel
Rachel Kim

Thanks, Rachel — helpful summary. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Token assumptions: the 1.2k tokens per invocation is a reasonable starting point. For conservative planning please run scenarios at 0.8k, 1.2k, and 2.0k tokens.
2) Volume: pilot floor = 150M/mo, target = 300M/mo, stretch = 500M/mo.
3) Budget band: our procurement lead gave me a working internal target of $8k–$18k/mo for pilot tooling (inclusive of invoicing/SLAs). We understand we may need to adjust with features/SLA.
4) CAC payback: preference is 6 months but can consider 9 months if tradeoffs are explicit.

Please include an explicit line itemized breakdown for: model cost, SLA/ops premium, storage/cache savings, and expected unit margin. Also loop procurement (Maya) — she will be our procurement lead for contracts and security questionnaires.

Maya — adding you here. Our procurement timeline is tight; if possible, can Redwood share a procurement checklist and typical contract milestones so we can map to our internal timeline?

Best,

Subject: Re: Post-call: inference margin playbook + next steps for 1M-token targets

Alex / Rachel — looping in a quick engineering-level sketch of cost assumptions we can use in the worksheet. I'll run the live numbers in the deep-dive but here are baseline inputs and levers: 

Baseline infra assumptions (hosted Redwood, multi-tenant w/ reserved capacity options)
- Raw GPU cost envelope (model-dependent): ~ $8–$20 / 1M tokens (varies heavily by model size and sequence length).
- Runtime + orchestration overhead (ops, autoscaling, KV cache management): add ~$3–$7 / 1M.
- SLA & support premium (24x7, dedicated routing, rapid fallbacks): typically +$10–$20 / 1M depending on response-time SLO.
- Net example: infra-only $12 / 1M -> list price with SLAs and support $32–$40 / 1M in many cases.

Levers that materially change $/1M
- Batching & concurrency tuning: can reduce per-token compute by up to 20–35% for high QPS patterns.
- KV/prefix caching: for repeat prompts or templates, effective tokens served can drop ~30–60% on cached flows.
- Quantized model variants: lower-cost variants yield 25–50% compute savings with modest quality tradeoffs.

Per-feature math example (illustrative)
- Avg tokens per invocation: 1.2k -> 833 invocations per 1M tokens.
- If list price = $40 / 1M -> cost per invocation = $40 / 833 ≈ $0.048.
- For 10k active users with 6 invocations/user/month -> 60k invocations -> monthly feature cost ≈ 60k * $0.048 ≈ $2.9k.

CAC/payback guidance
- If feature monetizes at $10/user/month and CAC is $240/user -> payback at 6 months requires gross margin to cover CAC and Opex. Example target gross margin 60–70% gives room for 6-month payback depending on monetization.

We should model 3 scenarios (conservative / expected / aggressive) with the worksheet. I can bring a short slide with sensitivity (tokens, caching, model variant) to show threshold points for margin and payback.

Happy to run numbers Wed afternoon — Rachel, what time worked for the customer?

—Karthik
